newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-KOURNIKOVA WINS, THEN ROASTS AGE RULES.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KOURNIKOVA WINS, THEN ROASTS AGE RULES.

text.p: The younger generation took centre stage on Thursday, as the $4.45 million Lipton Championships got under way with first-round action.
Anna Kournikova, the dynamic 15-year-old Russian, easily defeated Japan's Nana Miyagi 6-2 6-0 but saved her energy to complain about the age restriction rules on the women's tour.

Germany's 19-year-old phenomenon Nicolas Kiefer won his opening-round men's singles match with Dennis Van Scheppingen of the Netherlands, 6-2 5-7 7-6 (7-3). Australia's young hopeful Annabel Ellwood, 19, was also a first-round winner, beating Czech Denisa Chladkova 6-2 6-1.
Ellwood, currently ranked 74th, first grabbed headlines by ousting Jennifer Capriati in the first round of last year's U.S. Open.

Miyagi toppled Martina Hingis of Switzerland in Hingis's first match at the Lipton last year. Hingis, seeded 16th then, is the top seed this week and will automatically seize the number one ranking from Steffi Graf, not playing in Key Biscayne, on Monday, April 1.
Kournikova, ranked 90th, needed just 46 minutes of relentless groundstroking to eliminate Miyagi and was equally animated in the press conference afterwards.

A junior rival of Hingis but now well behind her in the rankings, Kournikova said she felt "frozen" by the age-limit rules -- designed to prevent teenage burnout -- which prevent her from playing more than 10 tournaments in the 12-month period between her June 7 birthdays.
"Other girls are playing 30 tournaments so they will do better than me even if I win all of my ten," she said. "I have no chance to play, especially if I draw a seed in the first round."

Kournikova did not turn professional in time to avoid the new regulations. Venus Williams and Hingis, both a year older than Kournikova, were "grandfathered" under the old system and can play more often. Kournikova will not be able to play an unrestricted schedule until she is 18, more than two years from now.

After being eliminated in the first round of the Australian Open, Kournikova penned her own letter of protest to the COREL WTA TOUR requesting a revision of the ruling. She has not received a response.

"I feel like I have to win every match," Kournikova said. "How can you learn how to play if you're not playing? I have to get match experience. I can't play junior tournaments for the next five years."
